newsitem.title: USA: MCI says could hike local network spending.
newsitem.headline: MCI says could hike local network spending.

text.p: MCI Communications Corp said Thursday it could boost its planned spending of $700 million on local phone networks this year if state phone regulators implement policies to promote local competition.
MCI's chief policy counsel, Jonathan Sallet, told a news conference that the number two long-distance carrier is "looking for the states to adopt pro-competitive policies."

In particular, he singled out the states following the FCC's currently suspended policy governing the pricing of "unbundled" elements of the local phone network -- such as call-switching devices and operator and directory assistance.

Under the FCC's policy, new competitors should be able to lease these components from local carriers at "forward-looking competitive prices to complete their own networks. The lease prices should be based on the cost of new and more-efficient facilities.
MCI plans to offer switched local service in 25 major U.S. markets by the end of the first quarter of 1997.
